brief:
Today, 13 November: nothing new is in the log since Legs A on 11 November, so this review repeats yesterday's and tonight is still Push B. If you trained Push B on 12 November and it did not save, open the app and check it is not sitting unsent; if you skipped it, tonight is that same Push B with the same numbers.

One program change today (version 11): on Legs A the calf press now goes second, straight after the leg press, on the same machine. On 11 November it was skipped while the hip machines after it were logged; the 3 November change said that would swap it to the calf machine this gym has, but the log does not say which one exists, so it moves to where a long night cannot push it off. Write which calf machine the gym has and the swap happens. Version 10 from 12 November stands: the crunch slot on both leg days is the ab crunch machine.

Where you stand: almost every lift that ran in the last week earned a step. Deadlift 240 for 6 on 10 November, so the next Pull A asks 250 for 5 at the top. Wide pulldown 127.5 for 11 and seated row 105 for 12 on all four sets earn 135 and 112.5 next Pull A. Dumbbell curl 30 for 10, 10, 10 earns 35. Leg press 200 for 10, 10, 10 and leg curl 150 for 12, 12, 12 on 11 November are both at the top of their ranges.

Tonight, Push B, in pounds. Dumbbell shoulder press: 50 for 9 on all four sets (you did 50 for 8 four times on 4 November). Machine chest press: 135 for 10, 150 for 10, then 165 for 8; you did 150 for 10, 10 on 4 and 9 November, and this machine has moved in 15-lb steps (105, 120, 135, 150). Dumbbell lateral raise: 15 for 15, three sets. Cable crossover high to low: 29 for 15, then 14. Reverse pec deck: the card shows 90 for 15, but you did 90 for 15 on all three on 9 November, so do the first set at 90 and the other two at the next weight up, and write that weight in the log; only 90 has ever been used on this machine, so the card cannot print the next one. Rope pushdown: 49 for 12, three sets. Last slot, still logged as Overhead db press: 50 for 12, two sets. After Push B comes Pull B, then Legs B.

Still open: whether that last Push B slot (Overhead db press, 50 for 12, 12 on 31 October and 4 November) is triceps or a shoulder press; one word in the note settles it, and if it is a press your triceps are at 6 direct sets, not 8. If tonight's log still has no note, the review by 16 November names it a dumbbell overhead press and puts two triceps sets back on Push B. Your logs through 11 November are stamped Meso 3, week 7, while the calendar says week 3 of the restarted block; if the phase tag at the top of the app is locked, the 25 November deload will not start by itself, and "Automatic (by date)" clears it. No bodyweight is logged since 23 August (207 lb). Conditioning: 2 to 3 low-intensity sessions of 20 to 30 minutes a week are allowed in the build block; nothing extra is asked tonight.

block.why: Today is the seventeenth day of the block restarted on 28 October at the New York gym (week 3 of 4); it builds to 24 November, deload runs 25 November to 1 December, assessment 2 to 8 December, prep from 9 December, show 108 days away. Nothing new has been logged since the 12 November review: the last night in the log is still Legs A on 11 November, and Push B, the session the 12 November review set, is not in the log. Either it was trained and has not saved yet (logs have landed a day late before), or it did not happen; either way the next session is still Push B, so this review repeats yesterday's on every muscle and lift and tonight's numbers are the same. The program changes in one place today, and not from new training data: the audit found that the 3 November calf rule fired on 11 November and was not carried out, so the calf press moves to second on Legs A (version 11). Session totals stay 19, 21, 20, 20, 21, 20. Everything else holds because no new evidence arrived: the lifts that ran in the last week nearly all earned a step (deadlift 240 for 6, wide pulldown 127.5 for 11, seated row 105 for 12 on all four, leg press 200 for 10, 10, 10, leg curl 150 for 12, 12, 12), which is what a build block should look like, and re-deriving the program from the same log would be churn. Next boundary is the deload on 25 November; the prep block is written at the assessment from what these four weeks log.

The four-week average done is 8: it averages the week of 19 October (one night logged, Pull A on 23 October at Vancouver), the week of 26 October (two deload days, then four nights), the week of 2 November (five nights) and this week (three nights so far), and counts half credit, so it sits under the 18 on paper mostly because of nights that did not happen, not because the sets on the card were too many.
